examFormat.rulesSummary: 2025–2027 syllabus · Core · no calculator · formula facts included · original full-length practice

title: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics (0580) · Paper 1 — original full-length mock (non-calculator)
subject: cambridge-igcse-mathematics-0580
instructions: Original full-length practice: 24 questions, 80 marks. This is not an official or endorsed Cambridge examination. Answer every question and all parts. Show your reasoning and calculations in the working canvas beneath each question; add pages when needed. Calculators are not permitted. Give exact answers unless a question specifies an approximation. Formula facts are attached to every question. Draw and label your own axes where requested; one grid square may represent the scale stated in the question. Use straight ruled lines and smooth curves as appropriate. Dimensions stated in a question are exact unless described as rounded. There is no separate reading period.

resources.label: Core formula facts
resources.text:
Mathematical formula facts — independently typeset for this practice paper
Triangle: area = bh/2 (b is the base, h the perpendicular height).
Circle: area = πr²; circumference = 2πr (r is the radius).
Cylinder: curved surface area = 2πrh; volume = πr²h.
Cone: curved surface area = πrl; volume = πr²h/3 (l is slant height; h is perpendicular height).
Sphere: surface area = 4πr²; volume = 4πr³/3.
Prism: volume = cross-sectional area × length.
Pyramid: volume = base area × perpendicular height / 3.

questions.label: Question 1
questions.prompt:
(a) Work out −7 + 12. [1]
(b) Work out 3² − 4 × 2. [1]

questions.label: Question 2
questions.prompt:
(a) Find the highest common factor of 18 and 30. [1]
(b) Find the lowest common multiple of 18 and 30. [1]

questions.label: Question 3
questions.prompt: Work out 2¼ − 5/6. Give your answer as a mixed number in its simplest form. Show your working. [3]

questions.label: Question 4
questions.prompt:
A coat costs $240 before a sale. Its price is reduced by 15%.
(a) Calculate the amount of the reduction. [2]
(b) Calculate the sale price. [1]

questions.label: Question 5
questions.prompt: Mina and Joel share 96 seedlings in the ratio 5:3. Find how many seedlings each receives. Show your working. [3]

questions.label: Question 6
questions.prompt:
(a) Round 0.04786 to two significant figures. [1]
(b) A length L cm is recorded as 24 cm, correct to the nearest centimetre. Complete the error interval: ___ ≤ L < ___. [2]

questions.label: Question 7
questions.prompt:
(a) Write 560000 in standard form. [1]
(b) Write 0.000720 in standard form. [1]
(c) Write 9.04 × 10³ as an ordinary number. [1]

questions.label: Question 8
questions.prompt:
(a) Write 2⁻³ as a fraction. [1]
(b) Simplify (3a²)². [2]

questions.label: Question 9
questions.prompt:
(a) Expand and simplify 3(2x − 5) + 4x. [2]
(b) Factorise fully 12y² − 18y. [1]

questions.label: Question 10
questions.prompt:
(a) Solve 3(x − 2) = 2x + 7. [2]
(b) Represent −2 ≤ t < 4 on a labelled number line. [2]

questions.label: Question 11
questions.prompt: Solve x + 2y = 17 and 3x − y = 9. Check your answer in both equations. [4]

questions.label: Question 12
questions.prompt:
The first four terms of a sequence are 7, 11, 15, 19.
(a) Write the next term. [1]
(b) Find an expression for the nth term. [2]
(c) Is 100 a term of the sequence? Explain your answer. [1]

questions.label: Question 13
questions.prompt:
For y = 2x − 3:
(a) Make a table of y values for x = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4. [1]
(b) On a square grid, draw and label axes with one square representing one unit. Plot your points and draw the line for 0 ≤ x ≤ 4. [2]
(c) State the gradient of this line. [1]

questions.label: Question 14
questions.prompt:
For y = x² − x − 2:
(a) Make a table of y values for x = −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3. [2]
(b) On a square grid with one square representing one unit on each axis, draw the graph for −2 ≤ x ≤ 3. [1]
(c) Use your graph to find both solutions of x² − x − 2 = 0. [1]

questions.label: Question 15
questions.prompt:
(a) ABC is an isosceles triangle with AB = AC and angle BAC = 38°. Find angle ABC and give a reason. [2]
(b) Find each interior angle of a regular hexagon. Show your method. [2]

questions.label: Question 16
questions.prompt:
A rectangular sheet is 12 cm wide and 8 cm high. A 4 cm wide, 3 cm high rectangular piece is cut from its top-right corner. Sketch the remaining L-shaped sheet.
(a) Find its area. [2]
(b) Find its perimeter. [2]

questions.label: Question 17
questions.prompt: A 13 m ladder rests against a vertical wall on horizontal ground. Its foot is 5 m from the wall. Find the height reached by the top of the ladder. Show your working. [3]

questions.label: Question 18
questions.prompt: Triangle ABC has vertices A(1, 1), B(4, 1), C(1, 3). Reflect the triangle in the vertical line x = −1. On a grid, draw the image and label its vertices A′, B′ and C′. [3]

questions.label: Question 19
questions.prompt:
A bag contains 5 red, 3 blue and 2 green counters. One is chosen at random.
(a) Find the probability that it is not blue. [1]
(b) The counter is replaced after every choice. Estimate the number of red counters chosen in 80 such choices. [2]

questions.label: Question 20
questions.prompt:
The numbers of visitors to a small exhibition on six days were 12, 15, 15, 18, 20, 28.
(a) Find the median. [1]
(b) Find the range. [1]
(c) Calculate the mean. [2]

questions.label: Question 21
questions.prompt:
A fair coin is tossed and a fair spinner numbered 1, 2, 3, 4 is spun.
(a) List all possible outcomes in a sample-space table. [2]
(b) Find the probability of a head and an even number. [1]
(c) Find the probability of a tail or the number 4, including when both occur. [1]

questions.label: Question 22
questions.prompt:
A train leaves at 0945 and arrives at 1215 on the same day. It travels 180 km and stops for a total of 15 minutes along the way.
(a) Find its average speed over the complete journey, including stops. [2]
(b) Find its average speed while it is moving. [2]

questions.label: Question 23
questions.prompt:
A sector has radius 6 cm and central angle 90°.
(a) Find its area in terms of π. [2]
(b) Find its perimeter in terms of π. [2]

questions.label: Question 24
questions.prompt:
For a rectangle that is not a square:
(a) State the number of lines of symmetry. [1]
(b) State its order of rotational symmetry. [1]
